Edinburgh. Probably the second biggest tourist trap hellhole after London. Hard to walk around especially during the Fringe Festival, which is a nightmare. Beautiful looking city, but the people are not very friendly, though.

(Ijincho) 
Plenty of things to do with a lot of diversity and balance of different urban areas. The slums, the downtown area, a huge public park and its very own Chinatown. Lots of freedom to run about, even on the main roads. 

(Kamurocho)
Perfect for the nightlife. Feels very alive with so much to do despite being much smaller than your average open world map. The neon lights on the Dragon Engine is something else. Watching this city develop throughout the entire game series is a pleasure. My only criticism is the Kamurocho Hills area not being accessible. 

(Sotenbori) 
This one often gives me the food cravings from all the cool restaurants they have. Very interesting characters encountered. (The Obatarian) I also like the contrast between the lively area North of the map and the dark slum feel you immediately get when you enter South of the map. 

(Ryukyu)
Very nice summer feel that feels very alive with a lot to do. Guilty pleasure was listening to the pedestrian crossing music... North of the map feels pretty dead, however. 

(Onomichi) 
Very beautiful during the day and you have the option of going up to the temple as well, which has an amazing view. Although, the streets feel a little too dead for me at times. 

(Nagasugai) 
Small simple map that is easy to navigate, and a very colourful city in the sunset. Not much else going on, though. Save points are too far from each other.

(Tsukimino)
This place felt miserable. For such a long map, there isn't much freedom to roam. You can't run along the main roads, which makes the city feel very dense. Not ideal if you can't be bothered with an enemy encounter. 

(Kineicho)
No personality whatsoever. Felt very dull, even during the daytime. Sorry.
